bib.title: OpenCodeInterpreter: Integrating Code Generation with Execution and Refinement

read.skipped: Appendix E/figure A3-A10 example dialogues skimmed (illustrative transcripts, no numbers); Figures A1/A2 are images with no text numbers.

question: Can fine-tuning open code LLMs on multi-turn dialogues containing execution and human feedback let them refine code iteratively at a level close to GPT-4 Code Interpreter?
hypothesis: Training on multi-turn data with execution and human feedback improves open-source models' ability to use feedback to fix code, narrowing the gap to proprietary systems.
contributions: Code-Feedback: 68K multi-turn interactions (192K turns) with execution and human feedback
OpenCodeInterpreter family (6.7B to 70B) fine-tuned on it
Evaluation of single-turn and multi-turn (execution feedback, synthetic human feedback, oracle) pass@1 on HumanEval/MBPP(+)

method.summary: Builds Code-Feedback by filtering 287K open-source coding queries to 156K hard ones, then converting them to multi-turn dialogues by single-turn packing, GPT-3.5/GPT-4 interaction simulation with executed code and simulated human feedback, deliberate-error code correction, and LeetCode similar-problem/follow-up grouping. Fine-tunes CodeLlama, DeepSeekCoder and StarCoder2 bases on Code-Feedback mixed 2:1 with WizardCoder 110K single-turn data, and evaluates with up to two refinement rounds.
method.task: code generation with iterative refinement from execution/human feedback

datasets.name: Code-Feedback
datasets.source: Built from Magicoder-OSS-Instruct, Python code ShareGPT, Magicoder-Evol-Instruct, Evol-Instruct-Code (287K queries; Qwen-72B-Chat complexity score 4-5 kept: 156K) plus LeetCode via TACO
datasets.preprocessing: Packing 16K samples (33.5K turns); Interaction Simulation 51K (155.5K turns); Code Correction 0.5K (1.2K turns); LeetCode Similar Problem 0.3K (0.65K turns); LeetCode Follow-Up 0.2K (0.76K turns); query filtering done twice with two prompts

datasets.name: HumanEval / HumanEval+ / MBPP / MBPP+ (EvalPlus)
datasets.source: Chen et al. 2021; Austin et al. 2021; Liu et al. 2023

models.name: GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-3.5 Turbo, Gemini Pro, WizardCoder, Magicoder, DeepseekCoder-Instruct, others

training.objective: supervised instruction fine-tuning on multi-turn dialogues (text says 'soft-target fine-tuning strategy' in ablation; undefined)

other.data_mix: WizardCoder 110K single-turn : Code-Feedback = 2:1 (Table 2 best); ablation ratios 2:1,1:1,1:2,1:3,1:5,0:1

inference.samples: 1 greedy sample per task; single run; pass@1
inference.prompting: Appendix D instruction prompt for first turn; refinement re-feeds solution and test results into the prompt

parameters.feedback_scenarios: execution feedback; synthetic human feedback (GPT-4, sees task, response, execution feedback); oracle (GPT-4 also sees ground-truth solution)
parameters.failure_feedback_types: exception message; not-expected (test inputs, expected, actual); timeout 'Execution timed out'

metrics.name: pass@1
metrics.definition: EvalPlus pass@1 on HumanEval/MBPP and plus versions; multi-turn: loop ends on pass or after 2 rounds

metrics.name: MT-Bench score
metrics.definition: GPT-4 scores 1-10 on 10 coding questions, first and second turn

eval.protocol: Baselines copied from EvalPlus leaderboard (10 Feb 2024) or rerun from official checkpoints; single greedy run, no seeds or confidence intervals; leakage checked by duplicate consecutive lines.

availability.code: open-sourced per ethics statement; site opencodeinterpreter.github.io

prompts.text: Rate the following code queries on a scale of 1 to 5 based on their complexity, where 1 is the easiest and 5 is the most difficult. Consider the complexity of the query

prompts.purpose: System prompt for multi-turn execution feedback simulation
prompts.text:
You are an AI code interpreter.
Your goal is to help users do a variety of jobs by executing Python code.

You are an exceptionally intelligent coding assistant that consistently delivers accurate and reliable responses to user instructions.
@@ Instruction
Here is the given code to do completion:

prompts.purpose: Synthetic human feedback with canonical solution (oracle)
prompts.text: You are tasked with providing guidance to a programmer who has drafted a code for a programming problem.
prompts.where: Appendix D; response limited to no more than three sentences

evidence.quote: The learning rate is set as 2e-5 with a 0.05 warm-up ratio and a cosine scheduler.

results.claim: OpenCodeInterpreter-DS-33B with execution feedback reaches 83.2 (76.4) average pass@1 on HumanEval/MBPP (plus), close to GPT-4 Turbo single-turn 84.2 (76.2).
results.setup: DeepSeekCoder-33B base fine-tuned; up to 2 refinement rounds with execution feedback; HumanEval and MBPP averaged; GPT-4 Turbo single turn baseline
results.quote: achieves an accuracy of 83.2 (76.4) on the average (and plus versions) of HumanEval and MBPP, closely rivaling GPT-4’s 84.2 (76.2)
results.note: Single-turn OpenCodeInterpreter-DS-33B Average is 79.0 (70.4); abstract compares the with-feedback number to GPT-4 Turbo without feedback.

results.claim: With GPT-4 synthesized human feedback, OpenCodeInterpreter-33B rises to 91.6 (84.6); this is the oracle setting where GPT-4 sees the ground-truth solution.

results.quote: further elevates to 91.6 (84.6) with synthesized human feedback from GPT-4
results.note: Non-oracle synthetic human feedback gives 88.0 (81.0); abstract does not say 91.6 is the oracle row.

limits: Authors concede performance may vary across languages and domains and may struggle with extremely complex or ambiguous intents (Limitations).
Case study Fig A10 failed: errors fixed incrementally and the maximum of three attempts exceeded.
Human-feedback and oracle runs only for 6.7B and 33B due to budget.
Evaluation limited to two refinement rounds; single greedy run, no seeds or intervals.
Baselines copied from EvalPlus leaderboard (10 Feb 2024) or rerun; execution-feedback baselines of other models were not trained for it.
Training data produced by GPT-3.5/GPT-4; 'human' feedback is simulated, oracle sees ground truth.
Batch size, optimizer, hardware and compute not reported; 'soft-target' fine-tuning undefined.
Authors acknowledge significant low-quality or incorrect data in the initial training set.
